Now that dotnet 11 is out, 
lets reimagine this whole project for dotnet 11 
if you were writing this project from scratch today 
what would you do differently? 
do that 
for example, 
don't worry about backward compatibility 
with older browsers 
this project only needs to work with the latest browsers 
we don't want to have any weird "compromises" 
unless absolutely necessary for the latest evergreen browsers 
if something exists only to shim for an older browser, cut it out 
and make our code cleaner and leaner 
there may be new things we could do in dotnet 11 and csharp 15
do them the new way when and where possible 
for example, I think we can get rid of most if not all `!important` in css 
or vendor prefixes like -moz- or -webkit- 
where evergreen browsers current stable might have moved on to non vendor prefixed ones
we only have one I think but I am using this as an example 
there might also be javascript and c sharp that we won't need with dotnet 11
also there might be nuget packages and github actions 
and other dependencies that we can upgrade to latest stable as well
upgrade them all 
as we do all of this 
please be mindful to use best engineering practices 
and solid principles 
Use your best judgment
If only a few files (under five or there about) need to change, give me the full path of the files that need to change and the FULL file 
if there are a lot of files that need to change 
Delivery
    Whole project as one tar.gz, unambiguous file placement
    do not include any file that has not changed 
    Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly
    No bespoke sed/patch scripts — full files only for anything that changes
    Docs updated alongside code changes
    Low verbosity, no code comments
    I only have the rc3 locally so the CI will need to do everything
    unless you can structure the global.json to work with rc3 or better
    this will improve soon when dotnet 11 stable lands on fedora default repos

Let me reconstruct the non-content files into a real tree.Extract into a fresh directory instead.

The tar.gz has 49 changed or new files, with paths relative to the repo root. Extract it over the repo: `tar xzf terlingua-dotnet11.tar.gz -C ~/src/dotnet/terlingua`.

**I couldn't build or test any of the C# here**, because this sandbox can't reach nuget.org or the .NET download servers. Your `dotnet test` with RC3 or the PR check will be the first real compile. I did check the JS: the rewritten syntax highlighter gives the same output as the old one on samples in 11 languages. I also checked in Chromium that the themes switch correctly in both light and dark OS mode.

**Delete these files:**
- `.nojekyll`. GitHub Pages doesn't run Jekyll when you deploy with Actions.
- `src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/404.html`. It was already overwritten in CI by the copy of `index.html`, so it never shipped.
- `src/ObserverMagazine.Web/libman.json`. It listed no libraries.

**Main changes**
- **Build:** targets `net11.0` and uses the C# 15 default. The ASP.NET packages are 11.0.0 and bUnit is 2.15.2; the others were already the latest. I removed two NuGet packages nothing used (`Microsoft.Extensions.Http` and `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Configuration`) and the duplicated central-package-management setting.
- **`global.json`:** pins `11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148` with prereleases allowed and roll-forward to later 11.0.1xx SDKs. Your RC3 SDK works locally and CI picks the 11.0.100 release. RC3 was an official Microsoft release, so its runtime packs should be on NuGet.
- **CI:** .NET `11.0.x` and Python 3.13. I removed the Node 24 workaround variable, the `//@` source-map line (old syntax) and the redundant content-processor arguments (they match the defaults). The audio cache copy no longer swallows errors. The action versions you had were already the latest.
- **`index.html`:** now contains no inline script. The theme API, highlighter, code-scroll and audio helpers moved into ES modules next to the components that use them. `OverrideHtmlAssetPlaceholders` fingerprints the Blazor script and fills an import map, so the modules are cache-busted on every deploy. A small `js/theme.js` still sets the theme before first paint.
- **Themes:** the System theme is now pure CSS using `light-dark()` and `color-scheme`. It follows OS changes live, and scrollbars and form controls match the theme.
- **CSS cleanup:**
  - Removed the `!important`, both vendor prefixes, the `vh` fallbacks and the deprecated `word-break: break-word`.
  - Dropped `overflow-wrap` declarations that `body` already passes down, and fallback values on variables that every theme defines.
- **Audio player:** removed the hidden fallback player, its 500 ms polling timer and about a dozen interop calls. The cause was `height: 2rem` clipping Chrome Android's native controls, so I removed that line instead. The player now stays hidden until the MP3 loads, so posts without audio no longer flash it. Speed values are formatted without depending on the browser's locale.
- **IndexedDB:** removed the open timeout and the `typeof indexedDB` guard, which only existed for older Safari.
- **C#:**
  - Collection arguments like `[with(StringComparer.Ordinal)]` and `[with(capacity: n)]` replace the old constructor calls.
  - `TelemetryService` uses the newer `Lock` type.
  - `AnalyticsService` takes `TimeProvider` instead of reading the clock directly.
  - The content processor returns an exit code instead of calling `Environment.Exit`.
- **Docs:** README and the About, Home and footer text now say .NET 11 and C# 15. README has a new Front end section.

I deliberately kept Python 3.13 rather than 3.14 because of the TTS dependencies, and stayed on KittenTTS 0.8.1 because version 2 reportedly comes with a licence you'd need to check.

Unrelated, but worth knowing: `wwwroot/plaintext/2026-04-26-zelensky.txt` looks like a full NYT opinion piece, and it's deployed publicly with the site.
